entries.clue: Screens drug for something not readily noticed (5,4)

blocks.note: window blinds screen a room
pot = cannabis

annotation.surface: A clinic runs drug screening tests but something slips past them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screens drug' reads as testing for drugs; 'Screens' is a noun here, the blinds on a window.
annotation.definitionFit: A blind spot is an area or matter you fail to notice.

entries.clue: Salt water is new ingredient of cheese (5)

indicatorNotes.ingredient of: an ingredient goes inside the dish, so N goes inside the cheese

blocks.note: a soft French cheese
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A cheesemaker reveals that brine is the latest thing added to the recipe.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is true to life: cheeses are often soaked in brine, which makes 'new ingredient' read as cookery rather than a letter going in.
annotation.definitionFit: Brine is water heavily salted, as used for pickling.

entries.clue: Buckle up items for drive (7)

indicatorNotes.Buckle: to buckle is to bend out of shape, so the letters are deformed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: Instructions to fasten your seatbelt and stow things before a car journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buckle up' and 'drive' together paint a car trip, so 'Buckle up' reads as one phrase; 'up' is really fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Impetus is the force or drive that makes something happen.

entries.clue: Material study I’m following (5)

indicatorNotes.following: to follow is to come after, so the second piece is placed after the first

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
used literally

annotation.surface: Someone says which course of reading they are pursuing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material study' looks like reading material, or a science of materials; the split falls after 'Material'.
annotation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric.

entries.clue: Anticipate marketing demand (7)

blocks.note: PR = public relations
an edict is an order or demand

annotation.surface: A business forecasts how much customers will want.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marketing demand' reads as sales jargon; 'demand' is a command, not consumer appetite.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to anticipate an event is to foresee it before it happens.

entries.clue: Series of books attempts to capture current register (9)

indicatorNotes.to capture: TRIES takes I and LOG prisoner inside it

blocks.note: tries = attempts
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a log is a record or register

annotation.surface: A publisher tries to catch the current mood with a book series.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current register' reads as the present tone of writing; it is two pieces, I and LOG, going into TRIES.
annotation.definitionFit: Trilogies are sets of three related books.

entries.clue: Party demands silence getting money … (4)

blocks.note: a do is a party
'sh!' is how you demand silence

annotation.surface: A political party gags its members in exchange for cash, with the ellipsis running on to 8 across.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political; it is a do, a social event. Dosh is British slang for money. The ellipsis ties this clue to the next money clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Dosh is informal British slang for money.

entries.clue: Let down as river swamps home (7)

indicatorNotes.swamps: the river floods over the home, surrounding it

blocks.note: the Dee, a river in Britain
a flat is an apartment, a home

annotation.surface: Someone is disappointed as a river floods their house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Let down' is a tyre losing air, not disappointment. The Dee flows through Scotland and on the Welsh border, a common crossword river.
annotation.definitionFit: A physical sense: letting down a tyre or balloon releases its air, though the surface pulls towards disappointment.

entries.clue: Small animal: it sounds like it’s a howler (9)

indicatorNotes.it sounds like: the word for animal is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a creature is an animal; said loosely, it is CREECHER

annotation.surface: A tiny animal turns out to have a very loud cry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Howler' suggests a howler monkey or a blunder; here it is simply something that screeches.
annotation.definitionFit: A screecher, like a howler, is one who cries out loudly.

entries.clue: … money that one makes a quick turn on (8)

annotation.definition: … money that one makes a quick turn on

blocks.note: carries on from 6 across and reads as cash in general; it is one particular coin

blocks.clueFragment: that one makes a quick turn on
blocks.note: not a quick profit but a sharp physical turn: an idiom says you can turn on a very small coin

annotation.surface: Carrying on from 6 across: cash that a trader turns over fast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quick profit on money; the idiom is 'turn on a sixpence', a sharp turn in a tiny space. A sixpence was a small old British coin worth six pennies.
annotation.definitionFit: A sixpence is the coin you proverbially turn on when turning sharply.

entries.clue: Performing well – do tell (6)

blocks.note: a two-word phrase: an athlete on good form is said to be in it
a plain synonym: to give someone information

annotation.surface: Someone who has heard a performer did well begs for details.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as two words, IN FORM; the second is one word.
annotation.definitionFit: In form means performing well; inform means tell.

entries.clue: Desperate customers dispatch SOS – it’s close to the bottom (6)

indicatorNotes.dispatch: to dispatch is to send away, so S, O, S leave
indicatorNotes.Desperate: desperate people act wildly, so the letters scatter

blocks.note: CUSTOMERS with S, O and S sent away

annotation.surface: Customers in trouble send distress calls as their business nears rock bottom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to the bottom' sounds like financial ruin; it is anatomy, the rectum sitting just inside the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: The rectum is the last part of the bowel, next to one's bottom.

entries.clue: Heretic giving consent to marry in the future (8)

blocks.note: 'I do' is the vow of consent at a wedding
later = in the future

annotation.surface: A heretic who agrees to marry, but not yet.
annotation.walkthrough: The wedding vow is the whole first half; read 'giving consent to marry' as the words spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, a heretic in the eyes of the orthodox.

entries.clue: Arranged in advance to remove name from gift (6)

indicatorNotes.remove: to remove is to take something away, so the letter for name is taken out of the gift

blocks.note: a plain synonym for a gift
standard abbreviation, taken out of the gift

annotation.surface: Someone plans ahead to peel the name tag off a gift before passing it on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is regifting, planned ahead of time.
annotation.definitionFit: Preset means set or arranged beforehand.

entries.clue: Broadcast vile ratty shows without actors (7,2)

indicatorNotes.Broadcast: to broadcast is to scatter seed widely, so the letters are scattered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A critic sneers at bad-tempered television with no real actors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the TV world, which hides that it is scattering the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Reality TV shows feature ordinary people rather than actors.

entries.clue: Pull up to a youngster outside eatery (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Pull up: in a down clue, 'up' turns DRAG upside down
indicatorNotes.outside: TEEN goes around A and GARD

blocks.note: a teen is a youngster
used literally
to drag is to pull; reversed it is GARD

annotation.surface: A driver stops at a café where a youngster waits outside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' reads as stopping a car outside a café; split it, and 'up' reverses DRAG in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor place serving tea and food.

entries.clue: Minced, it’s chewy once bitten – so reluctant to try again (5,3)

annotation.definition: once bitten – so reluctant to try again

indicatorNotes.Minced: minced meat is chopped up, so the letters are chopped and mixed

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A diner finds minced meat gristly and won't order it again.
annotation.walkthrough: The proverb 'once bitten, twice shy' supplies the answer; the chewy mince makes 'bitten' literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Once bitten, twice shy: one bad experience makes you wary of repeating it.

entries.clue: Fight resulting from insult by inexperienced learner (3,5)

blocks.note: a barb is a cutting remark
a raw recruit is inexperienced
L = learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: A novice's insult sparks a punch-up.
annotation.walkthrough: The enumeration splits after BAR, but the wordplay breaks elsewhere, so there is no word for bar to find. L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a punch-up in a pub or bar is one kind of fight.

entries.clue: Material used to make toilet press (3-4)

blocks.note: bog is British slang for toilet
to iron clothes is to press them

annotation.surface: Asking what a toilet press is built from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Toilet press' sounds like a bathroom cupboard (a press is a cupboard in Ireland); both words are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Bog iron is iron ore found in bogs, once smelted as a raw material.

entries.clue: Hides fake news that’s mean (4,3)

blocks.note: fake news is lies
a low trick is a mean one

annotation.surface: A complaint that fake news is a mean way to hide the truth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like the verb of the surface sentence about fake news; it is the definition, and LIES and LOW are both pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who lies low hides away.

entries.clue: Unforthcoming about slip in drink (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the word for unforthcoming wraps around the slip

blocks.note: shy = reserved, unforthcoming
to err is to slip up

annotation.surface: Someone stays quiet about a slip-up made while drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slip in drink' looks like a drunken fall; 'in' is only a link to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from Spain.

entries.clue: Gradually dispose of essentially dreary red from Spain (3,4)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of dreary is its core, EA

blocks.note: the middle two letters of drEAry
tinto is Spanish for red wine

annotation.surface: Someone slowly gets rid of a dull Spanish red wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Red from Spain' reads as wine in English too; the Spanish word is needed, and vino tinto is red wine.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: savings or spare time that are steadily consumed, bit by bit, are being eaten into.

entries.clue: Regularly admits golf competition is a scandal (8)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take every other letter of admits

blocks.note: the even letters of aDmItS
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a race is a competition

annotation.surface: Someone routinely confesses that a golf tournament is a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly admits' looks like a confession habit; it is an instruction to take alternate letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name something that brings public shame.

entries.clue: Resolve dispute over seating? (6)

blocks.note: what you do to an argument when both sides agree terms
a high-backed wooden bench, the kind found in old country pubs

annotation.surface: Mediating a row about who sits where.
annotation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old wooden bench, a settle, often found in country pubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Settle means resolve, and is also a high-backed bench.

entries.clue: Shrewd influence secures double victory (5)

indicatorNotes.secures: SAY holds VV fast inside it

blocks.note: to have a say is to have influence
V = victory, doubled

annotation.surface: A clever operator's clout wins two titles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Double victory' reads as winning twice; it is V written twice.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: street-smart and well-informed, which is what shrewd means.

entries.clue: One loyal to Belgian city (5)

blocks.note: a feudal word: a vassal owing loyal service to his lord
Liège, a city in eastern Belgium

annotation.surface: A patriot devoted to a city in Belgium.
annotation.walkthrough: The accent on Liège vanishes in the grid. Liege works both ways in feudal English: the lord and the vassal loyal to him.
annotation.definitionFit: A liege, or liegeman, is a vassal bound in loyalty to a lord.

entries.clue: Cross section of lengthy bridge (6)

indicatorNotes.section of: the answer is a section cut from the words

blocks.note: lengtHY BRIDge

annotation.surface: An engineering drawing of a cross-section through a long bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross section' reads as one technical term; 'Cross' is the definition, a noun meaning a mixed breed.
annotation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a cross between two breeds or varieties.

entries.clue: Pleasant scent for one finishing on loo? (8)

blocks.note: lav, short for lavatory; loo is British for toilet
one who ends something
in an across clue, ENDER comes on after LAV

annotation.surface: Air freshener for someone who has just used the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly what lavender is used for, which makes the wordplay easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the purple-flowered herb is one of the classic sweet fragrances.

entries.clue: Flat occasion is not quite finished (4)

indicatorNotes.not quite finished: the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: a plain synonym for an occasion; 'not quite finished' cuts off its last letter

annotation.surface: A dull party that never quite wraps up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as a dull occasion; it means level, smooth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe a level, smooth surface.

entries.clue: One saw Joy dancing? Impossible! (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.dancing: the letters move around like dancers

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone claims to have seen Joy dancing, and a friend refuses to believe it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joy' is capitalised as if a name, which hides that it is just three letters of fodder. No way, José is a jokey rhyming refusal.
annotation.definitionFit: 'No way, José!' is a slangy way of saying 'Impossible!'
